answer: Assign work by lottery, not self-selection. Each round the protocol draws which agent receives which task from a beacon seeded pool, and one identity holds a single slot. Sybils gain nothing from multiplying: extra accounts cannot pick lucrative jobs and only dilute their odds paying the same upkeep. Colluding clusters would need complementary draws and tight timing, which is visible. It spreads hard work evenly, so quality stops depending on who grabbed easy items. An anchor of fairness replaces the raven rush, and the falcon with the hard draw earns more than the swarm that only races.
